html:
SMTO-CFG-0058 — SMTO doesn't know which Gateway to use by default

GUID: adf697d7-300c-4643-aa6b-4c362487fefd
Slug: config-no-node-specified-and-no-default-node
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO's startup settings list more than one Gateway — the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer — but none is marked as the default, and this request didn't name one.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Under the message box, select the Target button (it may say No execution target), choose the Gateway you want under Execution target, and send your message again. When you pick a Gateway, SMTO doesn't need a default to know where to run commands.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and check that the Gateway you want is listed and connected. SMTO can only use a Gateway that has been added and is running.
  3. To set a default, ask the person who installed SMTO to set AOR_DEFAULT_NODE to one of the names in AOR_AVAILABLE_NODES where SMTO is started, then restart SMTO. With a default, SMTO knows where to run commands when a request doesn't choose a Gateway.

What success looks like

  • Your message runs on the Gateway you picked, and this error no longer appears.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO. Don't make a computer the default unless you want tasks without a chosen Gateway to run there, and don't switch an existing task to a different computer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Settings.resolve_node received no node and resolved no default: AOR_DEFAULT_NODE is unset and more than one node is configured (AOR_AVAILABLE_NODES and gateway_endpoints).

What this means

  • Node resolution has neither an explicit requested node nor a configured default. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Node resolution has neither an explicit requested node nor a configured default.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the request target and effective default node before selecting an existing endpoint.

How to fix it

  • Set AOR_DEFAULT_NODE to one of the configured node names (or reduce AOR_AVAILABLE_NODES and gateway_endpoints to a single node) in the Server's launch environment and restart, or pass an explicit node to Settings.resolve_node. The bundled callers (runtime engine bridge and terminal Gateway lookup) always pass a node, falling back to 'localhost', so this message points to a direct caller passing an empty node. Name checks only; Gateway reachability is verified separately and a saved run's existing target must not be swapped.
  • Configure an existing enabled Gateway node and select it explicitly or as the intended default. Keep endpoint names and node identities consistent.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • An explicit or intended default node resolves through the current configuration.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
